tasks.spec:
Your current working directory IS a git worktree of the podcast repo. Edit files there directly. Do NOT git commit, branch, push, or stash; leave changes uncommitted. Do not call any MCP tool or App and do not capture anything to an external system.

HOW YOU WILL BE GRADED, stated up front so you are not guessing. A checker runs after you and fails you for any of these:
- changing a file outside your owned list (below);
- changing production code and adding no tests;
- adding fewer than 6 new `def test_...` functions;
- adding no NEGATIVE test, meaning nothing in your diff uses pytest.raises, asserts a blocked or failed result, or otherwise proves a guard stops bad input;
- the test suite not passing.
There is no document or summary format requirement. Write notes or none.

YOUR OWNED FILES, the only paths you may touch:
  server/pipeline/orchestrator.py
  tests/test_orchestrator.py
  tests/test_orchestrator_grid_wiring.py
  tests/test_orchestrator_gate_wiring.py
  tests/test_media_gates_integration.py
  tests/test_keep_timeline.py

BACKGROUND. This repo produces a two-person video podcast. Every episode begins as four separate WebM files from a Daily.co room: host camera audio, host camera video, guest camera audio, guest camera video. They do not share a zero, and each can contain dropouts where packets stopped arriving. Historically the pipeline computed episode timing three incompatible ways and nothing compared them, and five consecutive renders shipped broken as a result.

THE GRID-AWARE PATHS ALL EXIST AND ARE TESTED. Previous work built them additively, defaulted OFF, so nothing calls them yet. YOUR ENTIRE JOB IS TO TURN THEM ON, together, in the orchestrator. You are not designing anything new; you are connecting finished parts.

THE EXACT APIS AVAILABLE TO YOU, read each function before calling it:

  av_sync.write_timeline(raw_dir, output_path, *, stems_dir, include_screen_tracks)
  av_sync.build_stems(raw_dir, processed_dir, timeline, roles)
  av_sync.verify_stem_content_pin(timeline, stems_dir)
  av_sync.derive_timeline(raw_dir, *, include_screen_tracks)

  video_assembly.composite_side_by_side(host_video, guest_video, host_audio, guest_audio,
      output_path, offsets, *, stems_mode, timeline_identity)

  angle_render.angle_switch_edit(host_video, guest_video, host_audio, guest_audio,
      composite_path, offsets, transcript_path, out_path, content_end, hop_s, dead_air,
      editorial_cuts, *, input_timeline, camera_holes, camera_hole_t0_s,
      camera_dropout_threshold_s)
  angle_render.GRID_ALIGNED_STEM_INPUTS        # the input_timeline value for stems
  angle_render.CAMERA_DROPOUT_SWITCH_THRESHOLD_S   # 5.0, the owner's setting

  interview_transcription.transcribe_interview(assets, episode_dir, model, *,
      word_timestamps, require_gpu, source_mode, timeline_path, strict_filename_offsets)
  interview_transcription.STEM_GRID_SOURCE_MODE

  media_gates.validate_raw_source_integrity(paths, *, min_decoded_s, pts_gap_pct,
      expected_tracks, enforce_divergence)

WHAT TO WIRE, in this order:

1. BUILD THE MASTER AS A PIPELINE STAGE. After the raw tracks are downloaded and after any reconnect stitching, and BEFORE anything consumes them, derive the timeline and build the four stems into the episode's processed directory. Include screen tracks. Record it as a stage with a receipt the way existing stages do; follow the surrounding pattern rather than inventing one.

2. VERIFY THE PIN BEFORE EVERY CONSUMER. verify_stem_content_pin distinguishes three outcomes: matched, mismatched (a stem changed under the timeline), and missing (a stem is absent, or the timeline predates pinning). Matched proceeds. Mismatched and missing must BOTH halt. Missing is not a pass. Record the result as a gate receipt.

3. COMPOSITE READS STEMS. Call composite_side_by_side with the four STEM paths and stems_mode=True, passing the timeline identity. The stems already contain their leading placement, so no per-track offset may be passed in this mode; passing one applies the delay twice, which is a bug that already shipped once on this episode. Read composite_side_by_side to see exactly what it expects in stems mode.

4. ANGLE RENDER READS STEMS ON THE GRID. Call angle_switch_edit with the stems and input_timeline set to GRID_ALIGNED_STEM_INPUTS. Pass the camera hole list from the timeline plus its t0, and the 5-second threshold constant, so the owner's rule is active: when one participant's camera is inside a dropout longer than 5 seconds, the other participant's angle is forced for that span. Nothing is ever cut by this; only which camera is shown changes.

5. TRANSCRIPT READS STEMS. Call transcribe_interview with source_mode set to STEM_GRID_SOURCE_MODE, the timeline path, and strict filename offsets enabled. This is what stops transcript timestamps being up to 76.86 seconds early on a track with a dropout.

6. DIVERGENCE ENFORCEMENT ON STEMS ONLY. validate_raw_source_integrity takes enforce_divergence and it defaults to False deliberately: a RAW track that lost packets has huge divergence by construction, so enforcing it on raw input would block almost every genuine recording. Stems are different: they are hole-filled and equal length, so divergence near zero is the correct expectation and a non-zero value means a stage removed time. Enforce it when validating STEMS. Do not enable it for raw.

CONSTRAINTS.
- The raw path must remain reachable and working. Put the new behavior behind a switch that defaults ON for complete two-participant interviews, and make sure solo and incomplete-asset episodes still take their existing path. If you cannot determine an episode's shape, halt rather than guessing.
- Never remove time from one track without removing it from all four. Nothing in this wiring should cut anything.
- Every halt must record a receipt saying which check failed and why, following the existing gate-receipt pattern in this file.

TESTS ARE THE DELIVERABLE AS MUCH AS THE CODE. At minimum prove: the master stage runs and produces a timeline plus stems; a MISMATCHED pin halts; a MISSING pin halts; the composite is called in stems mode with no per-track offsets; the angle renderer is called with grid input and the 5-second threshold; the transcript is called in stem-grid mode; divergence enforcement is on for stems and off for raw. Mock the heavy media calls; do not require real ffmpeg work.
tasks.verified: the grid paths are switched on together in the orchestrator, pin mismatch and missing both halt, and at least 6 new tests including negatives prove it
